Based on the provided healthcare Q&A matches, it appears that well-differentiated small hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is not considered a "clinically early" cancer. In fact, there was no significant difference in disease-free survival between patients with well-differentiated HCC and those with low-grade HCC (liver dysfunction diagnosed).

However, this does not necessarily mean that HCC cannot be considered clinically aggressive or potentially life-threatening. The question seems to imply that even well-differentiated HCC can have a poor prognosis.

It is essential to consider the context of liver disease progression and the various factors that influence the prognosis of HCC patients. While low-grade HCC may not have the same risk as advanced stages, it can still be a sign of an underlying process leading to more aggressive disease.

In summary, the prognostic information available suggests that well-differentiated small hepatocellular carcinoma is not considered clinically early cancer. However, this does not necessarily rule out the possibility that HCC can have a poor prognosis in certain contexts. Further research and clinical evaluation are necessary to fully understand the relationship between liver disease progression and the prognosis of HCC patients.
